main_text.p: strum, castellum: pizpur, specula; pizrteal, propugnaculum.
ꝏ icte, Holera: & wortt herba. Inde ꝏ irtefpurgum, Herbipolis]Eâdem notione Saxon. pyprʒ: unde hortus eis pyprun?

ꝏ ithersacco, Adversarius, quasi wedersaeb, aut wiedersagger] Eodem sensu Sax. piprpraca, quod etiam contradictorem notat, à piperprace, contradictio.: voce compositâ à piper, contra, adversus, & recʒan, (nobis to sap) dicere, vulgò hodie gatnsap.
ꝏ ittt, Prudentia] Vide ꝏ ewitt.

ꝏ ittuf, Lex: & wittute, lege: & wittuteʒagbere. legislator. A promulgando, & longè latéque spargendo] Malim ego à witt, Sax. piт, & ʒepit, sapientia, prudentia; quia leges sunt prudentum confulta, vel decreta. Unde prudentum in eam rem consessus Sax. dictus piвenaʒemoт, quasi sapientum conventus, à piвena, & ʒemoт, ita significantibus ꝺꞩagbere autem hic, in wittut ꝺꞩagbere, à Teuton. ꝺꞩaegben, quod ferre sonat.

page.notes: Several Saxon glosses are set in black letter or are very small; marked forms are doubtful. The handwritten "241" in the right margin is not printed text and is omitted. Marginal dagger-like cross marks (ꝏ) stand for printed reference symbols. The line "nibus" at the foot is the continuation of "Saxonibus" printed at the right, partly cut off.
